arguments.rule_content:
rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Packed {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic packed Cobalt Strike payloads - prone to false positives with .NET assemblies"
        author = "SOC Team"
        confidence = "medium"
        false_positives = ["Packed legitimate .NET applications, Microsoft signed binaries"]
        remediation = "Consider hashing out known-good files; use in conjunction with network IOCs"

    strings:
        $a = { 4D 5A } // Standard PE header
        $b = "beacon" wide ascii
        $c = { FF D5 } // call ebp

    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and filesize < 2MB and all of them
}

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) resulted in the compromise of a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The attacker leveraged malicious PowerShell execution from Outlook to deploy a ShadowPad variant via process hollowing and rundll32. C2 communication was established over HTTPS to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) and a suspicious domain (update.ns3.ezdns.cc). Indicators confirm the use of TTPs including T1566.001 (Phishing), T1218.011 (Signed Binary Proxy Execution), T1071.001 (Web Protocols), and T1055.012 (Process Hollowing). Lateral movement attempts were detected via SMB to a file server. The host was isolated via firewall block, but EPP scan failed to detect the in-memory implant. Full containment requires host reimage and credential rotation.

arguments.summary: Post-exploitation activity detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14) under user CORP\jsmith. Initial access achieved via phishing email triggering encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook. The attacker deployed a malicious DLL using rundll32.exe from the Temp directory, establishing a Cobalt Strike beacon to C2 server 198.51.100.23:443. Lateral movement observed via SMB to internal hosts including a file server (10.0.5.50). Credential access attempts and WMI-based remote execution targeting a domain controller were identified in sandbox-omitted behavioral data. Containment actions included blocking C2 IP at firewall and disabling the compromised user account. Eradication involved full endpoint scan and automated system hardening via Ansible playbook.

Containment: User account CORP\jsmith disabled
